subject: Architecture
title: Taipei 101: Beating the Wind and Quakes
description: A quick, practical guide to Taipei 101: Beating the Wind and Quakes.

hook.text: Taiwan faces typhoons and earthquakes. Building the world's tallest tower there seemed insane.

buildup.text: Taipei 101 rises 1,671 feet in one of the planet's most seismically active zones.

discovery.text: A 730-ton steel pendulum hangs near the top, swinging to counteract wind sway. Visitors can watch it move.

twist.text: The building survived a magnitude 6.8 earthquake during construction — a crane fell, but the structure held.

climax.text: Its bamboo-inspired segmented design isn't just decorative — each section resists wind independently.

punchline.text: Nature sends typhoons and earthquakes. Engineering sends them back.

quiz.question: What does the 730-ton pendulum inside Taipei 101 do?
options: Generates electricity from the building's movement
Swings to counteract wind sway and stabilize the tower
Anchors the building to bedrock during earthquakes

details.summary: Taipei 101, completed in 2004, was the first building to exceed 500 meters and was designed to withstand typhoons and earthquakes in one of the world's most seismically active regions. A 730-ton tuned mass damper suspended near the top counteracts wind and seismic sway.
details.whyItMatters: Taipei 101 proved that supertall buildings could be built safely in extreme seismic and wind zones. Its engineering solutions expanded the geographic range of where the tallest buildings could be constructed.
takeaways: First building to exceed 500 meters, completed in 2004
A 730-ton tuned mass damper counteracts wind and seismic sway
Designed for extreme typhoon and earthquake conditions

faq.question: How does a tuned mass damper work?
faq.answer: A massive steel sphere suspended on cables swings in opposition to the building's movement. When wind or an earthquake pushes the building one way, the damper's inertia pulls it back. Taipei 101's 730-ton damper is visible to visitors and has become a tourist attraction.

faq.question: Has Taipei 101 survived major earthquakes?
faq.answer: Yes. During a 6.8 magnitude earthquake in 2002 while still under construction, a crane fell from the upper floors but the structure performed as designed. The building has weathered multiple typhoons and moderate earthquakes since completion with minimal damage.
